mcqs.question: In an isobaric expansion, 2.5 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K expands from 10 L to 30 L against an external pressure of 1 atm. If the internal energy of the gas increases by 5 kJ, what is the amount of heat absorbed (q) during the process? (Take 1 L·atm = 101.3 J)
mcqs.explanation: Work done by the system: w = -PΔV = -1 atm × (30 L – 10 L) = -20 L·atm = -20 × 101.3 J = -2026 J = -2.03 kJ. Using the first law ΔU = q + w, we have q = ΔU – w = 5 kJ – (‑2.03 kJ) = 7.03 kJ ≈ 7.0 kJ. Hence option A is correct. The other options either ignore the work term or use the wrong sign.

mcqs.question: A chemical reaction occurring in a sealed container releases 150 kJ of heat to the surroundings while doing 40 kJ of work on the surroundings. According to the first law of thermodynamics, what is the change in internal energy (ΔU) of the system?
mcqs.explanation: The first law states ΔU = q + w. Heat released by the system is negative: q = –150 kJ. Work done by the system on the surroundings is also negative: w = –40 kJ. Therefore ΔU = –150 kJ + (‑40 kJ) = –190 kJ. Option A correctly reflects this calculation; the other options misuse the signs.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly applies the relation ΔU = q + w?

options.A: For an exothermic reaction, q is negative, so ΔU is always negative regardless of work.
options.B: For an endothermic reaction, q is positive, so ΔU is always positive regardless of work.
options.C: ΔU equals the sum of heat exchanged (q) and work done (w); both signs must be considered.
options.D: Work done on the system is always positive, therefore ΔU is always positive.

mcqs.answer: ΔU equals the sum of heat exchanged (q) and work done (w); both signs must be considered.
mcqs.explanation: The first law requires adding the algebraic values of heat (q) and work (w). Whether ΔU is positive or negative depends on the combined effect of both terms. Options A and B ignore the contribution of work, and D misstates the sign convention for work. Hence option C is the only correct statement.

mcqs.question: A gas is compressed from 5 L to 2 L at a constant external pressure of 2 atm. What is the sign of the work (w) done on the system?
mcqs.explanation: Work on the system is defined as w = -PΔV. Here ΔV = V_final – V_initial = 2 L – 5 L = –3 L. Substituting, w = - (2 atm)(‑3 L) = +6 L·atm, which is positive. Therefore the work done on the system is positive. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because the sign can be determined from the given data.

mcqs.question: Process A: An ideal gas expands isothermally at 300 K from 5 L to 15 L against a constant external pressure of 1 atm. Process B: The same gas is compressed isobarically at 1 atm from 20 L to 5 L. Which process involves a greater magnitude of work (|w|)?
mcqs.explanation: Work magnitude is |w| = P|ΔV|. For Process A, ΔV = 15 L – 5 L = 10 L, so |w_A| = 1 atm × 10 L = 10 L·atm. For Process B, ΔV = 5 L – 20 L = –15 L, so |w_B| = 1 atm × 15 L = 15 L·atm. Because 15 L·atm > 10 L·atm, Process B has the larger magnitude of work. Options A and C are therefore incorrect, and D is false because both processes involve work.

mcqs.question: When 1.0 g of hydrogen gas at 298 K is burnt in excess oxygen at constant volume, the temperature of the calorimeter rises from 298 K to 301 K. The calorimeter has a heat capacity of 2.5 kJ·K⁻¹. Assuming complete combustion, calculate the enthalpy change (ΔH) per mole of H₂ in kJ·mol⁻¹. (Molar mass of H₂ = 2 g·mol⁻¹)
mcqs.explanation: Heat released: q = CΔT = 2.5 kJ·K⁻¹ × (301 K – 298 K) = 7.5 kJ (negative because the system loses heat). This amount corresponds to 1.0 g of H₂, i.e., 0.5 mol. Therefore per mole, ΔH = (‑7.5 kJ) / 0.5 mol = ‑15 kJ·mol⁻¹. Option A matches this value. The other options either miss the division by moles or use the wrong sign.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the first law of thermodynamics?

options.A: Energy can be created but not destroyed.
options.B: The total energy of the universe remains constant.
options.D: Heat always flows from a hotter body to a colder body.

mcqs.explanation: The first law states that the change in internal energy of a system (ΔU) equals the heat exchanged with the surroundings (q) plus the work done on the system (w). Option C is the precise mathematical statement. Options A and B are vague or incomplete, and D describes the second law, not the first.

mcqs.question: A system absorbs 200 J of heat from the surroundings and does 50 J of work on the surroundings. What is the change in internal energy (ΔU) of the system?
mcqs.explanation: Using ΔU = q + w. Heat absorbed is positive: q = +200 J. Work done by the system on the surroundings is negative: w = –50 J. Thus ΔU = 200 J + (‑50 J) = +150 J. Option B is correct. Options A, C, and D either add the work incorrectly or use wrong signs.
